newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian bank governor sees mergers in sector.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian bank governor sees mergers in sector.

text.p: Lithuanian central bank chief Reinoldijus Sarkinas said on Thursday that market forces and mergers would reduce the number of commercial banks operating in the Baltic state.
"The number of banks in Lithuania will decrease...the market will determine the situation," Sarkinas told a news conference.
"A process of merging is inevitable," he added.

The small Baltic state which quit the Soviet Union in 1991 is still recovering from a crisis which rocked its infant commercial bank sector late last year with the surprise closure of two of its top commercial banks.
The crisis has shaken public and investor confidence in the country's banks and economists predict that it growth could be slowed as a result.

A fresh crisis in the sector was recently averted when the government agreed to bail out the troubled state-run State Commercial banks, which faced a liquidity crunch caused by a crippling bad loan portfolio.
Six small banks recently had their licences revoked as the central bank tightens its capital adequacy and liquidity requirements.
The country currently has 14 banks operating, including three large state-run banks.
